articles.title: Bears kicker goes viral after trying to trip Packers receiver who decked Chicago coach on sideline

paras.en: The Green Bay Packers-Chicago Bears rivalry is one of the best in football, and one viral moment added to it during the Packers’ 31-7 beatdown at Lambeau Field over their NFC North foe in Week 5.
Packers receiver Matthew Golden fielded a punt by the Bears toward the end of the first half, and after returning it 17 yards, he ran out of bounds on the Chicago sideline.
Still running at full speed, Golden crashed into an unsuspecting Bears coach, who went tumbling to the ground after the blindside hit.
Bears kicker Cairo Santos seemed to witness the act by Golden, and his reaction was one some fans on social media called dirty.

As Golden ran back onto the field, Santos clearly tried to trip the second-year receiver before he got between the white lines. Santos was unsuccessful, but as the broadcast caught the entire act from Golden hitting the Bears coach to the attempted trip, it quickly went viral on social media.
Fans started a discourse over which action was more dirty, and you can suspect where Packers and Bears fans aligned their views.
In the end, no flags were thrown for either player and the half came to an end.
After the game, Golden admitted to Santos trying to trip him, but took the high road when asked about the incident.
"Yeah, he did. He did. But it’s all good. I ain’t got nothing to say to him," Golden said.

The 23-year-old Texas product, whom the Packers took in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft, caught six passes from quarterback Jordan Love for a career-high 123 yards, including a 50-yard snag to help Green Bay humble the Bears.

And while Golden took the high road, his teammates weren’t as humble. Linebacker Zaire Franklin took aim at Bears receiver Luther Burden III, suggesting that he "ain’t wanna play anymore" and that he "quit today."
This was a response to Burden saying that Chicago wanted to "beat them real bad and make them quit" prior to their latest meeting.

As divisional foes, they will meet once more this season, with a Christmas Day tilt scheduled in Chicago. By then, playoff implications could be at stake, which would heighten the tension even more between these bitter rivals.
As things stand after Week 5, the Minnesota Vikings lead the NFC North at 5-0, while the Packers, Bears and Lions are all 3-2 on the year.

articles.title: Bills-Rams delivered every ounce of Super Bowl LXI preview talk as overtime thriller deserves a rematch

paras.en: All week, the talk surrounding "Monday Night Football" between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams was the potential that this would be a preview for Super Bowl LXI.
If this does indeed come to fruition, football fans will be mighty happy because this game was cinema in Inglewood on Monday night.

A back-and-forth battle that saw 35 total fourth-quarter points, an overtime period filled with clutch plays, and more led the Bills to beat the Rams, 37-34, to improve to 4-1. The Rams fell to 2-3, a record nobody predicted through their first five games, but they are still a top NFC contender.
In a game filled with offensive fireworks from both Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford, it was Rams defensive captain Nate Landman who came through with the most important play of the game in overtime.

Allen and the Bills got right into Rams territory on the opening drive thanks to Khalil Shakir’s 57-yard catch-and-run on second-and-long. On the very next play, James Cook, who had two touchdowns but a fumble earlier in the game, wasn’t cautious with the football when he got the handoff from Allen. Landman punched at the ball, knocked it clean out of Cook’s arms, and his teammate landed on it.
Instead of the Bills getting the potential game-winning score, Stafford and the Rams had a chance to go downfield and win it all thanks to Landman’s efforts.

Stafford did just that, using his star receiver Puka Nacua, who exploded for 17 catches on 25 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown, to get into field goal range for kicker Harrison Mevis to try a 48-yard field goal for the win.
But just when it seemed one team would finally come away with the win and get the final word, the other team stepped up.

The Rams have dealt with special teams woes in recent seasons, and Mevis, who had missed a 50-yarder earlier in the game, had his game-winning field goal blocked. The game remained tied, and the Bills’ offense breathed a sigh of relief knowing they could rectify Cook’s mistake.

Allen took matters into his own hands, rushing for 32 yards on the drive and getting well within field goal range for Tyler Bass to get his shot at glory. The snap was clean, the kick was true, and the Bills celebrated a hard-fought victory that had football fans thinking about the Martin Scorsese "ABSOLUTE CINEMA" meme (if you don’t know that one, look it up).

This game truly had it all, especially in the fourth quarter where, just to get to overtime, Stafford had to lead his third straight touchdown drive with 1:39 left on the clock and one timeout. He didn’t even need the timeout, as he found Davante Adams for his second touchdown of the game on a perfect route that left him wide open.

Rams head coach Sean McVay elected to go for the tie with an extra point instead of going for a two-point conversion. He had tried earlier at that, but the Rams failed to convert after Stafford was sacked.

In the box score, Allen threw for 210 yards with one touchdown and one interception, while rushing for a game-high 121 yards on just 10 carries with his score. Cook finished with 111 yards on the ground with his two touchdowns, while both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum scored for the Rams.

From the stars showing up under the bright L.A. lights to the beautiful scoring dance between these two high-octane offenses, to key plays flipping momentum left and right, this game deserves another meeting for the Vince Lombardi Trophy.
It was football entertainment at its finest and lived up to every ounce of the hype.

articles.title: Protester punched in face by Trump supporter, mocked by president at Ohio rally: 'Gotta go on a diet'

paras.en: A heckler wearing a "Release the Epstein Files" shirt was punched in the face by an apparent supporter of President Donald Trump during a rally Monday in Youngstown, Ohio, before the president mocked the protester's weight.

Trump was criticizing Ohio Democratic Senate candidate Sherrod Brown, who is challenging Republican Sen. Jon Husted after losing his Senate seat in 2024, when rally attendees shifted their attention toward a confrontation in the crowd.
Video of the confrontation showed a rallygoer who appeared to support Trump shoving the heckler and striking her in the face as the crowd chanted "USA!"
The man also grabbed the woman by the hair and attempted to slam her face toward the ground.

Police eventually intervened and broke up the fight before escorting the woman out of the venue. Video showed the man who struck her remaining in the arena and exchanging high-fives with other attendees.

Trump appeared to notice the disruption and accused the protester of being paid to interrupt the rally, although he offered no evidence to support the allegation. He also mocked the protester's weight.

"He's a paid protester," Trump said, appearing to be unaware that the heckler was a woman. "They’re all paid. They get paid by the lefties in order to destroy our country. They’re scum. But he’s going back home to Mom. He’s going back home to Mom. Look at him. Look at him. Terrible. Don’t we love law enforcement? Oh, he’s gotta go on a diet! He’s a fat guy. Wow. Wow. Gotta go on a diet fast. We all do."
"No, they’re paid protesters. That’s a very low-class protester," the president added.

The woman's "Release the Epstein Files" shirt comes as Trump and his Justice Department face bipartisan scrutiny over the delay in the release of additional documents related to the investigations into deceased sex predator Jeffrey Epstein.
Just days before the fight on Monday, there was a fight at another Trump rally in San Antonio, Texas, where a man wearing a MAGA hat grabbed a heckler by the hair and pulled him to the ground.

articles.title: Card surcharge ban used as ‘cover’ for larger price increases by Australian businesses, experts say
articles.author: Patrick Commins and Jonathan Barrett

paras.en: Businesses are using the recent ban on credit card surcharges as “cover” to pass along much larger price increases to customers, experts say, as cafes and restaurants struggle to cope with climbing costs and rising interest rates.

Credit card surcharges, typically worth about 1.5% of the transaction, were banned from 1 October, as part of a Reserve Bank-led reform aimed at improving transparency for customers and, ultimately, lowering bank fees.
Small Flat White, an online coffee price tracker, has reported that 17% of cafes have increased their prices since the start of the surcharge ban.
Of those who raised coffee prices, the average increase was 50c, or more than 10%, according to the survey of more than 1,500 cafes.
That is multiples of the typical 1.5% card surcharge fee.

Stephen Wu, an economist at investment bank UBS, said resilient consumer demand and a high inflation environment “may be allowing merchants to use the change as ‘cover’ to pass through broader cost pressures”.
“Following years of above-target inflation, consumers may be more accepting of price rises,” Wu said.
“Evidence of ‘round-up’ pricing in items such as coffee suggests pass-through could exceed the surcharge itself.”

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has warned businesses that they must not “mislead consumers” by claiming a price rise is due to the surcharge ban when the increase also reflects other costs.
The ACCC has also said that businesses who try to avoid the ban by describing the surcharge as another type of fee or charge “may be engaging in misleading conduct”.
Wes Lambert, chief executive of the Australian Restaurant & Cafe Association, said business costs were rising rapidly while coffee prices in Australia were among the lowest in the world.
Lambert said businesses changed their prices for many reasons, and that the surcharge ban could have been the impetus for company owners to build up the courage to pass on costs to customers.
“Maybe this is the catalyst that has caused cafes and restaurateurs around the country to wake up.”
Lambert said restaurants were blaming the need for price rises on higher produce costs, steep rents and recent adjustments to junior pay rates and awards.
Many business owners are also affected by the four interest rate rises in 2026, which have driven up repayments on variable-rate loans and equipment financing.
“It should be no surprise that in a high inflation, high interest rate environment that businesses are going to raise their prices,” he said.
Despite being telegraphed well in advance, the surcharge ban has triggered a furious response from small business groups.
The treasurer, Jim Chalmers, was forced to intervene after the Australian Taxation Office announced it would no longer accept credit card payments for tax owing.
Chalmers said the government would provide additional funding to the ATO to cover the cost of the surcharge until the middle of next year.
Despite the furore, Morgan Campbell, the head of policy at consumer advocate group Choice, said: “I don’t think there’s any shock in the way this is working”.
“There was always an acknowledgement that some businesses would put up their prices. But consumers are better off knowing the price up front,” Campbell said.
He said it was too early for Choice to begin its own research on how the surcharge ban was working.
“Some of this will take some time to wash through the system,” he said, noting the RBA expected businesses to put more effort into finding lower cost bank providers.
If some businesses are putting up their prices by much more than the surcharge, Campbell suggested it was up to customers to decide how to respond.

articles.title: Tuesday briefing: Could Burnham take Britain back towards the EU?
articles.author: Hettie O'Brien

paras.en: Good morning. After a holiday spent contracting nursery bugs from an 11-month-old, it’s good to return. Yesterday, Andy Burnham marked his first day back after party conference by calling for a closer relationship with the EU and drawing a line under a decade of “drift and division”. On Sunday, he said it was “clear” the Kremlin had been involved with the 2016 Brexit referendum vote.

Both statements mark a break, rhetorically at least, from his predecessors. Conservative governments long insisted there was no evidence of Russian interference in the Brexit vote. Keir Starmer attempted to put the entire issue of Brexit behind him, treating it as a historic event rather than a cause of economic pain.

- UK | Andy Burnham said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps were “almost certainly” behind threats to RAF Fairford, the firmest attribution of responsibility made so far by the UK after an incident late last month.
- UK politics | A close adviser to Nigel Farage had an influential role at a national polling company despite not being publicly associated with the firm, the Guardian revealed.

- Ukraine | Volodymyr Zelenskyy has vowed to respond to Russia’s continuing attacks on the Ukrainian power grid as European leaders rally around Kyiv amid a feud with Donald Trump over Ukraine’s strikes on oil refineries.

- Israel | Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered the country’s attorney general and the head of the Shin Bet security service to reveal the identities of soldiers and officers interviewed in the documentary NAZA and prosecute them for causing “harm to Israel’s diplomatic and security interests”.
- US news | RJ Mitte, the young actor best known for playing Walter White Jr in the award-winning TV series Breaking Bad, died on Monday. He was 34.
In depth: What does Burnham want from Europe?

In the years after it voted to leave the European Union, Britain became something of a laughing stock among EU member states. “It was like a box set TV drama. People in Brussels would be staying up to watch votes in the House of Commons,” Jennifer Rankin, who moved to Brussels to cover the EU for the Guardian in January 2016, tells me. Civil servants in Brussels grew to regard the UK as one might regard a belligerent and ungrateful elderly relative, an impression that reached its apotheosis when the former Northern Ireland secretary Brandon Lewis admitted that the UK’s Brexit arrangements for Northern Ireland would break international law (albeit in a “very specific and limited way”.)
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “From 2016 to 2020, the UK was seen as a model of how not to run your country,” Jennifer says. This impression softened after the passing of the Withdrawal Agreement Act in early 2020, and the Windsor framework deal, which amended the arrangements under the Northern Ireland protocol in 2023. “That was a turning point in drawing a line under the bad blood of the Brexit years,” Jennifer says. Keir Starmer’s government then sought to cooperate with the EU on various issues such as security, food and fishing, but the “reset” he pledged to deliver was tightly circumscribed by his red lines: no rejoining the single market, no customs union, no freedom of movement.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: After his conference speech, Burnham suggested he might be open to reconsidering this when he suggested, somewhat cryptically, that the UK could go “all the way” (presumably towards full EU membership), and yesterday he called for a “longer-term discussion” about Britain’s relationship with the EU. But what might that actually mean?

Burnham has been “showing a lot of ankle” to remainers over the last few weeks, Peter Walker tells me. During his Labour conference speech, he promised to lay out “different options” for Britain’s long-term relationship with Europe, and acknowledged that Brexit had caused “more harm than good”.

“It’s pretty clear that a decent majority of people would like to push a switch that meant Brexit had never happened,” Peter says. Indeed, a YouGov poll in January 2025 found that just 11% of people thought Brexit had been more of a success than a failure. And as recently as last week, the Messina Group, a polling company, reported that half of voters say they would like to rejoin the EU. The economic consequences of Brexit are now well known, and research has estimated that, a decade after the referendum, UK GDP per head is between 6% and 8% lower than it would have been without Brexit. Yet reversing this decision would require another referendum, which would be politically fraught, reigniting a debate that splintered the country a decade ago, and reducing a highly complex and technical issue to a binary decision.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: It’s hard to imagine Burnham – or any politician, for that matter – wanting to fight the next election while pledging something so divisive. Notably, even the Liberal Democrats, the most pro-EU of the major parties, favour rejoining the single market and customs union but describe UK membership of the EU as a “long-term goal” rather than an immediate priority.

If a second referendum seems like a vanishingly distant prospect, other changes could take place without one. In the combustive years after Brexit, there was a short-lived hope that the UK might pursue its own version of the Norway model, allowing it to become a member of the European Economic Area. “It was the Conservatives who decided to pursue the hardest Brexit possible,” Peter reminds me.

In theory, a softer deal could mean rejoining the single market and customs union. But this would mean breaking Labour’s red lines, which Burnham has said he will stick to. And if the UK was to rejoin the single market but remain outside the EU, it would be forced to accept rules that it had no power to shape. “As soon as you look at the democratic deficit that comes with single market membership, the case for rejoining the EU becomes stronger,” Jennifer tells me.

The debate over rejoining the EU is often conducted in relatively parochial terms, as if it only concerns Britain. But the UK’s future relationship with the EU will be largely shaped by the member states of a union that has changed significantly since the referendum. Far-right parties are gaining power in France and Germany, while the mercantilist politics of China and the US have inspired the EU’s Made in Europe agenda, a series of protectionist laws designed to bolster European industry and reduce reliance on Chinese imports.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In this context, Burnham may decide it’s better to be inside the tent than outside it. The Made in Europe agenda is particularly concerning for the government, since UK industry could suffer if exports were legally classified as “non-European” goods under these new laws. But as Mujtaba Rahman wrote in an interesting opinion piece for the Guardian in July, “any serious rejoin debate must start from an honest assessment of what the EU has become”.

Right now, the longer term outcome is anyone’s guess. In his statement to the Commons, Burnham confirmed that the planned UK-EU summit will go ahead in November. Negotiators are expected to discuss a trade deal on food and drink, a deal on emissions trading, a plan to link the energy systems of the EU and UK and the new youth mobility scheme. These areas were all discussed at last years’ UK-EU talks, so Burnham wasn’t announcing anything we didn’t already know.

“There’s a lot of frustration in Brussels that the UK has been talking a big game on a reset with the EU, without actually changing very much,” Jennifer says. “The theme over the last ten years is that the EU has always been waiting for the UK to define what it wants. The rhetoric may be warmer, but the substance has stayed the same.”

- Here’s a line I didn’t expect to read today: professor Devi Sridhar, chair of global public health at the University of Edinburgh, is worried about the pneumonic plague (although it might not be for the reasons you suspect). Poppy
- Kiran Sidhu was touching, on considering who to pass her most prized possessions down to in her will since she doesn’t have children. Poppy

- I, too, have been had by the myth that my (small amount of) muscle will turn into fat if I don’t force myself into a few push-ups every week. Not so, according to this week’s Is it true that … column – although what does happen when you stop exercising isn’t that much more reassuring. Poppy
Cycling | Matt Richardson has been withdrawn from the Great Britain team for next week’s World Cycling Championships in Shanghai amid allegations of misconduct.

Football | Almost half of female footballers are considering leaving the sport because of financial concerns or psychological stress, and 57% have struggled with their mental health, according to a report highlighting the working conditions for players worldwide.

Sport | Manchester United have endured their worst league start in 40 years but coach Michael Carrick insists he does not feel under pressure and has said his captain, Bruno Fernandes, will rediscover his form.

The Guardian leads with “PM: Britain’s relationship with EU ‘not good enough’”. The i has “Burnham ready to sign new EU deal next month – as he attacks Brexit ‘damage’”. The Mail says “Burnham in retreat over Russia Brexit ‘lies’”.

The Times splashes on “Cut screen time in class ‘for sake of pupil health’”. The Financial Times has “Putin breaking ‘ceasefire’ on energy targets, says Zelenskyy”. The Mirror reports on comments from Reform’s Robert Jenrick on migrants, under the headline “Horrifying”.
Trump rewards Putin and betrays Ukraine with Russia diesel deal

Donald Trump’s deal to buy Russian diesel has been met with fury from Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said it was ‘a weak decision’ and would generate ‘billions’ in extra revenue for Putin’s war effort. The Ukrainian president has also rejected US calls for an ‘energy ceasefire’, which would require Kyiv to stop striking oil refineries, saying Moscow must first end its attacks on energy infrastructure. Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s senior international correspondent, Luke Harding.
A bit of good news to remind you that the world’s not all bad

The Naffah family has been making church bells in the Lebanese town of Beit Chabab for three centuries. Led by master bell-maker Naffah Naffah and his two sons, their workshop is the last remaining production centre for church bells in Lebanon and the only source of church bells for much of the Middle East.

Crafted using a mix of modern and ancient tools, each bell takes about two months to make and bears the names of those who worked on it. Naffah and his sons Charbel and Youssef are determined to preserve the tradition. Charbel will succeed his father as master of the workshop and Youssef helps alongside studying medicine, but says he would take Charbel’s place if needed.
“Traditions are important to us,” he says. “We are living and breathing tradition here in this workshop.”
And finally, the Guardian’s puzzles are here to keep you entertained throughout the day. Until tomorrow.

articles.title: Same-sex couple sue over Slovakia’s refusal to register marriage
articles.author: Rob Cameron in Bratislava

paras.en: A same-sex couple are suing authorities in Slovakia for refusing to register their Austrian marriage, testing whether a landmark EU court ruling can turn recognition abroad into legal security at home.
Their fight exposes a clash between European obligations and national restrictions – and what that means for LGBTQ+ people living under Robert Fico’s populist-nationalist government.
Ivan Novotný, 31, and Metod Špaček, 51, married in Austria in 2020, but six years on, their marital status at home remains unrecognised.
There is no same-sex marriage in Slovakia, a socially conservative, predominantly Catholic country; neither is there any form of civil partnership.

But Novotný and Špaček, who are both lawyers and former diplomats, are not asking for that. They want the Slovakian authorities to recognise a marriage that was concluded legally in another EU country – something the bloc’s top court has said is mandatory for all EU members.

“I’ve said this publicly several times, and [LGBTQ+] activists in Slovakia have criticised me for it: Metod and I are not discriminated against here. We have a lovely life here in Bratislava, in Slovakia,” Novotný said. “So, we don’t actually need [recognition of marriage] for our day-to-day lives.”
For example, said Novotný, when Špaček was hospitalised during the Covid pandemic he was treated by a “lovely” doctor who recognised Novotný’s official relationship to her patient.

He added: “She put me down on the report as ‘husband’ and gave me all your [Špaček] medical information. The problem is: that was because she was nice, not because she had to do it. If someone wanted to make trouble for us, they could do it.
“That’s not how the rule of law should work.”
The couple argue they are on solid legal ground after a ruling by the EU’s highest court in November 2025 in response to a case brought by a Polish same-sex couple who had married in Berlin.

Jakub Cupriak-Trojan and Mateusz Trojan had challenged the Mazovia provincial governor’s refusal to recognise their German marriage. The court ruled that member states must recognise such marriages where couples had exercised their right to move and reside in another EU country, and created or strengthened family life there.
The European court of justice ruling does not require member states to allow same-sex weddings at home.
The Slovakian authorities explained why Novotný and Špaček’s request to register their Austrian marriage had been turned down in a letter signed by the interior minister, Matúš Šutaj Eštok.

“[The letter] says that since the constitutional definition of marriage [in Slovakia] is a bond between a man and a woman, they lack the legal basis for formally recognising the marriage certificate. That’s essentially it,” said Špaček, who served as chief of staff to the country’s liberal former president Zuzana Čaputová.

Across town, in the house his grandparents built on a hill overlooking the Danube, Marián Žáry Kukelka, 44, recalled his wedding to his partner, Ondrej, in 2023. The couple married in Hainburg an der Donau, an Austrian town visible from their terrace.

Žáry Kukelka, a radio presenter for the public broadcaster STVR, is also suing Slovakian authorities. He uses his full married name on air (Žáry is Ondrej’s surname) and is supported by his colleagues. But his official documents refer to him as Marián Kukelka. He said: “It’s a court case for love. I don’t need that surname to live my life, but for me it’s a kind of tribute to my partner, that I can carry his surname too.”.
Žáry Kukelka lives behind Bratislava Castle, not far from Zámocká street – the scene of the homophobic attack in 2022 where two people were shot dead outside the LGBTQ+ bar Tepláreň.
The anti-LGBTQ+ rhetoric of many Slovakian politicians, especially in the government, was contributing to an atmosphere of increasing hostility, he said.

Last year, Fico’s government backed constitutional changes recognising only two sexes and tightening adoption restrictions. Žáry Kukelka told the Guardian that Hainburg an der Donau had been “overwhelmed” with LGBTQ+ couples from Slovakia wanting to get married since a change to Austrian legislation made it possible.
He himself had experienced little in the way of abuse as a gay man, he said, although he admitted he thought carefully before using the words “my husband”, depending on whom he was talking to.
“Two weeks ago, we were in Switzerland, and there we held hands in public for the first time in a long time,” he said. “We felt it was different there.”
Slovakia’s interior ministry said it was bound by the country’s existing constitutional and legal framework, regardless of whether a marriage was valid abroad.

It acknowledged the primacy of EU law but argued that recognition for freedom of movement purposes did not require registration as a marriage. Its administrative work “cannot replace decisions by the legislature or the constitutional legislature,” the ministry told the Guardian.

articles.title: Russia's offensive ability is broken, Kyiv's former top general tells BBC

paras.en: Ukraine has stabilised the front line and "broken Russia's ability to advance" by killing so many of its men, Ukraine's former commander-in-chief has said in an interview with the BBC.
Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi made the comments in an exclusive interview, his first since he was dramatically forced from his post in the summer.
He addressed his sacking, disagreeing with his critics who declared him too "old school" to command Ukraine's new, technologically advanced forces.

He also pushed back against allegations made by soldiers who previously served under him, who told the BBC they were ordered to remain at their positions even when they were almost surrounded by Russians, leading to high losses.
Syrskyi said that Moscow's overall losses in the war were six times higher than Ukraine's. "If you count only dead, then it's up to 11 times," he added.

Neither Russia nor Ukraine officially release the numbers of their dead. Ukraine's military says it inflicted record losses this year on Russian soldiers in September, although that cannot be verified.

UK intelligence chiefs estimate Russia has lost around half a million men killed in Ukraine since launching its full-scale invasion in 2022. The US-based Center for Strategic and International Studies meanwhile believes, external Ukraine has lost up to 150,000 troops killed by June 2026.

He says this difference in death toll â as well as technological advances, and a strategy of attacking weak points in Russia's lines while containing their advances in other parts â accounts for the current stalemate at the front.
In the first six months of 2026, Russia managed overall to seize 61 sq km, the general said. "It's an indication that the front line has been stabilised."
The Institute for Study of War (ISW) has also confirmed this trend. One of its recent reports, external says that in September 2026, Moscow lost more territory than it took.

Syrskyi was appointed Ukraine's commander-in-chief in 2024. He had previously won praise for defending Kyiv at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, and for leading the successful counteroffensive east of Kharkiv in the autumn of that year.
But President Volodymyr Zelensky fired Syrskyi this summer, amid a major disagreement with then-defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov.
Fedorov had said that instead of adapting to the realities of the changing war, the army under Syrskyi had blocked his initiatives.

Zelensky initially fired Fedorov, as tensions burst into the open between the two men. But mass street protests then forced the president to also fire Syrskyi, replacing him with Maj Gen Mykhailo Drapatyi, 43.
Syrskyi told the BBC that he had "disagreements" with Fedorov because the latter "didn't take into consideration the interests of the army" when procuring weapons and supplies.

Fedorov had created an "imbalance" in supplies, Syrskyi said. He had prioritised drones while overlooking key front-line kit such as unmanned ground vehicles, pick-up trucks and motorbikes. Even with drones, Syrskyi said, there were shortages as the army got only half of what they needed.

Fedorov was a popular young minister who was known for his digital and technological initiatives. Many contrasted him with Syrskyi, who critics thought was not fit to lead the new technological arms race with Russia.

But Syrskyi disagrees with such criticism. It was during his time the use of drones reached this new, unprecedented level, including deep strikes more than 2,000km (1,200 miles) behind enemy lines, he said. Ukraine was the first country to create the Unmanned Systems Forces as a separate branch of armed forces, under his command: now, he said, drones account for 80% of Russia's losses.
Under his military leadership, however, Ukrainian troops undertook chaotic withdrawals from the eastern cities of Avdiivka and Vuhledar, and from around Pokrovsk.

Soldiers who spoke to the BBC in the past complained that they were ordered to remain at their positions at any costs. By the time they were told to pull back, it was often too late as they were almost surrounded by Russian troops.
Syrskyi does not deny that such situations occur on the front line. But he told the BBC that Ukraine was fighting against a far more powerful army.

In 2025, the ratio of jets and bombs was 18 to one in Moscow's favour, he said. In the same year, Russia had two-and-a-half times more artillery pieces and shells than Ukraine. And with four million militarily trained men who they can mobilise, Russian forces can create chances to push through, he argued.

One of Syrskyi's most famous operations was an incursion into Russia's Kursk region that started in August 2024. It ended with a dramatic retreat the following spring, which some soldiers described as "catastrophic". Syrskyi, however, insisted that the Kursk operation was "a necessity".
"In the summer 2024, Russian forces were pushing along all main directions on the front line with up to six times more troops than we had," he explained.
The Kursk incursion disrupted Russia's offensive and forced Moscow to redirect troops, giving Ukraine a respite and a chance for its stretched brigades in the east and south to recover, Syrskyi said.

He also had strong words for European allies who doubt that Russia may have territorial ambitions beyond Ukraine. He advised European partners to start preparing for the war now and "drop all illusions that [it] will not come".

He also said he believed Ukraine's war was going to become even more technological. There will be more robots, automated systems and artificial intelligence (AI). "Even ordinary weapons now get an AI-based control system to enhance their capabilities," he said.
Such technologies can give a new life to conventional weapons like tanks. Both Russia and Ukraine were now racing to develop "active systems of defence" to protect armoured vehicles, Syrskyi said.
But he insisted that "the human role will remain definitive [on the battlefield] because [people] will need to control those systems".

articles.title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

paras.en: Americans head to the polls on 3 November to decide how the rest of Donald Trump's presidency will play out.
paras.zh: 美国人将于11月3日前往民意调查，以决定唐纳德·特朗普总统任期的其余部分将如何发挥作用。

paras.en: Thousands of races are taking place across the US, at different levels of government. But the main event for voters will be electing members of the House of Representatives and the Senate, the two chambers that make up Congress.
paras.zh: 在美国各地，成千上万的种族在不同级别的政府中发生。但选民的主要活动将是选举众议院和参议院的议员，这两个议院组成了国会。

paras.en: Both of them are currently controlled by the Republicans, the president's party. The success or failure of Trump's final two years in office could rest on the outcome.
paras.zh: 两人目前都由共和党控制，共和党是总统的政党。特朗普最后两年任期的成败可能取决于结果。

paras.en: Here's our visual guide to where the battle for power will be won and lost - from approval ratings, to key races and issues and the huge amount of money being spent.
paras.zh: 这是我们的视觉指南，从支持率、关键比赛和问题以及花费的巨额资金到权力争夺战的胜负。

paras.en: One of the reasons the opposition Democrats have a chance to take back Congress is the president's low approval rating, which is a good indicator for how well his party could perform.
paras.zh: 反对党民主党有机会收回国会的原因之一是总统的支持率较低，这是他的政党表现如何的一个很好的指标。

paras.en: He began his second term as president with an approval rating of just over 50%, according to polling resource website Silver Bulletin, but it quickly fell into the 40s.
paras.zh: 根据民意调查资源网站Silver Bulletin的数据，他以超过50 ％的支持率开始了他的第二个总统任期，但很快就落入了40多岁。

paras.en: It was hovering around 42% when Trump decided to launch air strikes with Israel against Iran at the end of February this year but it fell below 40% shortly afterwards. It is currently sitting at about 37%.
paras.zh: 今年2月底，当特朗普决定与以色列对伊朗发动空袭时，这一比例徘徊在42%左右，但此后不久就降至40%以下。目前约为37%。

paras.en: Eight years ago, Trump's approval rating was significantly higher at this point in his first term, at 43%. Joe Biden's at the same point in his term was at 40%. In both cases, the sitting president lost control of the House in the midterms but kept hold of the Senate.
paras.zh: 八年前，特朗普第一个任期的支持率明显更高，为43%。乔·拜登（ Joe Biden ）在任期的同一时间点是40 ％。在这两种情况下，现任总统在中期选举中都失去了对众议院的控制权，但仍然控制着参议院。

paras.en: But Trump's poor ratings help explain why Democrats are hopeful of winning both chambers of Congress and why they are setting their sights on states that Republicans have won consistently in recent years.
paras.zh: 但特朗普糟糕的评级有助于解释为什么民主党人希望赢得国会两院，以及为什么他们将目光投向近年来共和党人一直赢得的州。

paras.en: The current Republican majority in the House of Representatives, the lower chamber, is as thin as it gets - they have 218 representatives, which is the exact number needed to have control, plus one independent who votes with them.
paras.zh: 众议院（下议院）目前的共和党多数席位非常薄弱--他们有218名代表，这是控制权所需的确切数字，加上一名与他们一起投票的独立人士。

paras.en: Members of the House serve a two-year term so all 435 seats are up for election in November.
paras.zh: 众议院议员任期两年，因此所有435个席位将于11月举行选举。

paras.en: But most districts are not considered competitive because the party that holds them has such solid support that there is only one likely winner.
paras.zh: 但大多数地区不被认为具有竞争力，因为持有它们的一方拥有如此坚实的支持，以至于只有一个可能的赢家。

paras.en: The Cook Political Report, which analyses campaigns and elections, suggests that just 21 districts are "toss-ups" that could be won by either party.
paras.zh: 分析竞选和选举的库克政治报告显示，只有21个地区是任何一方都可能赢得的“折腾”。

paras.en: Of those 21 toss-ups, 15 are currently held by Republicans and six by Democrats. If the Democrats win five of those on top of 28 districts classed as likely or leaning Democratic, they will win the House.
paras.zh: 在这21个抛掷中， 15个目前由共和党人持有， 6个由民主党人持有。如果民主党在28个可能或倾向于民主党的地区中赢得5个，他们将赢得众议院。

paras.en: Historically, the midterms see a high number of seats changing hands in the House, usually in a protest against the White House. The average number lost by the president's party is 27, according to data, external going back to 1934. Of those 23 elections, the president's party has only made gains in three.
paras.zh: 从历史上看，中期选举中有大量席位在众议院易手，通常是为了抗议白宫。根据数据，总统政党的平均损失人数为27人，外部追溯到1934年。在这23次选举中，总统所在政党仅在3次选举中获胜。

paras.en: The Republicans have a slightly stronger hold on the Senate. They hold 53 of the 100 seats while the Democrats have 45 and two independents who also vote with them.
paras.zh: 共和党对参议院的控制力略强。他们在100个席位中占有53个席位，而民主党有45个席位，两名独立人士也与他们一起投票。

paras.en: Members of the Senate serve six-year terms so roughly a third are up for election every two years.
paras.zh: 参议院议员任期六年，因此大约三分之一的议员每两年选举一次。

paras.en: Thirty-five seats are up for grabs in November but analysis by the Cook Political Report suggests that only seven of them are toss-ups that could go either way.
paras.zh: 11月份有35个席位可供争夺，但《库克政治报告》的分析表明，其中只有7个席位是可以任意颠倒的。

paras.en: Of those toss-ups, six are currently held by Republicans and one by Democrats. The Democrats would need to win four of those seats, plus the four classed as likely or leaning Democratic, to hit 51 and take control of the Senate.
paras.zh: 其中六个目前由共和党人持有，一个由民主党人持有。民主党需要赢得其中4个席位，再加上被归类为可能或倾向于民主党的4个席位，才能达到51个席位并控制参议院。

paras.en: But winning a majority is no easy task for the Democrats.
paras.zh: 但对民主党人来说，赢得多数席位并非易事。

paras.en: They need to keep hold of their seat in Michigan, where polls suggest the race is tighter than Democrats would like between Abdul El-Sayed, a left-wing political outsider, and his Republican rival Mike Rogers, a Trump ally and former FBI agent.
paras.zh: 他们需要保持在密歇根州的席位，在那里，民意调查显示，左翼政治外来者阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德(Abdul El-Sayed)和他的共和党对手、特朗普的盟友、前联邦调查局特工迈克·罗杰斯(Mike Rogers)之间的竞争比民主党人更激烈。

paras.en: And they would also need to pick up seats in states that Trump won by double-digits in 2024, including Alaska, Iowa and Ohio.
paras.zh: 他们还需要在2024年特朗普以两位数获胜的州获得席位，包括阿拉斯加州、爱荷华州和俄亥俄州。

paras.en: But polls suggest they have a chance, even in Texas where former teacher James Talarico could become the first Democrat to win a Senate seat in the state since 1988 if he defeats Ken Paxton, the current state attorney general and close Trump ally.
paras.zh: 但民意调查显示，即使在德克萨斯州，前教师詹姆斯·塔拉里科（ James Talarico ）如果击败现任州检察长、特朗普的亲密盟友肯·帕克斯顿（ Ken Paxton ） ，也可能成为自1988年以来第一位赢得该州参议院席位的民主党人。

paras.en: Trump pledged to "end inflation and make America affordable again" in his 2024 election campaign but the cost of living crisis is proving to be the key issue for voters.
paras.zh: 特朗普承诺在2024年的竞选活动中“结束通货膨胀，让美国再次负担得起” ，但生活费用危机被证明是选民的关键问题。

paras.en: The president proudly declared that gas was "now below $2.30 [Â£1.74] a gallon in most states" in his State of the Union address on 24 February. But the war with Iran began four days later, disrupting Middle Eastern energy supplies and causing gas to hit $4 (Â£3.03) in the US.
paras.zh: 总统在2月24日的国情咨文演讲中自豪地宣布，天然气“现在在大多数州低于每加仑2.30美元[1.74英镑]”。但与伊朗的战争在四天后开始，扰乱了中东的能源供应，导致美国的天然气价格达到4美元（ 3.03英镑）。

paras.en: The war became increasingly unpopular as its consequences reverberated around the world and ultimately hit American consumers in the pocket. One poll carried out in August found 63% of respondents disapproved of Trump's handling of the situation.
paras.zh: 这场战争变得越来越不受欢迎，其后果在世界各地引起反响，最终冲击了美国消费者的口袋。8月进行的一项民意调查发现， 63%的受访者不赞成特朗普处理这种情况的方式。

paras.en: Other issues that voters say are important to them include healthcare and immigration.
paras.zh: 选民认为对他们很重要的其他问题包括医疗保健和移民。

paras.en: Trump has recently touted his policies around immigration as a big success, citing significantly lower border-crossing figures than in recent years.
paras.zh: 特朗普最近宣称他围绕移民的政策取得了巨大成功，理由是过境人数比近年来大幅减少。

paras.en: Many Democratic candidates are focusing on the high costs of US health insurance and the impact of Trump's legislation on access to the healthcare system.
paras.zh: 许多民主党候选人正在关注美国医疗保险的高成本以及特朗普立法对医疗保健系统的影响。

paras.en: Most signs point towards a successful midterms for the Democrats, but it wouldn't be the first time that Trump and his party have outperformed polls if they do win more seats than expected.
paras.zh: 大多数迹象表明，民主党的中期选举将取得成功，但如果特朗普和他的政党赢得比预期更多的席位，这并不是第一次超过民意调查。

paras.en: One of the few things in their favour is their huge financial advantage.
paras.zh: 对他们有利的少数几件事之一是其巨大的经济优势。

paras.en: At the end of August, the Republican National Committee and its allied groups had more than $600m (Â£455m) cash on hand, while the Democrats had just under $400m (Â£303m).
paras.zh: 截至8月底，共和党全国委员会及其联盟组织手头现金超过6亿美元（ 4.55亿英镑） ，而民主党手头现金略低于4亿美元（ 3.03亿英镑）。

paras.en: On top of that, the Republicans also had more than $400m held by Trump's MAGA Inc group, the main fundraising and spending arm of the "Make America Great Again" political movement.
paras.zh: 除此之外，共和党人还拥有特朗普的MAGA集团持有的4亿多$ ，该集团是“让美国再次伟大”政治运动的主要筹款和支出部门。

paras.en: The Republicans are using that financial advantage to buy advertising.
paras.zh: 共和党人正在利用这种财务优势来购买广告。

paras.en: More than $1bn worth of political ads were broadcast to US voters in September, according to research firm AdImpact, external. Republicans spent $200m more than the Democrats and outspent them in nearly all of the Senate races classed as toss-ups.
paras.zh: 根据研究公司AdImpact的数据， 9月份向美国选民播放了价值超过10亿美元的政治广告。共和党人比民主党人多花了2亿美元，并且在几乎所有被归类为折腾的参议院竞选中都超过了他们。

paras.en: Trump will be hoping this late messaging blitz can help convince Republicans to get out and vote in November, boosting turnout and limiting the damage done to him and his party.
paras.zh: 特朗普希望这次晚些时候的消息闪电战能够帮助说服共和党人在11月退出投票，提高投票率并限制对他和他的政党造成的损害。

paras.en: Whatever the result, attention will quickly turn to the next presidential election in 2028. Trump's unpopularity has dominated the midterms, but with him constitutionally unable to run for a third term the focus will shift to what the Democrats stand for, not just what they stand against.

articles.title: Death threats and isolation - the cost of fighting sexual violence in Iraq

paras.en: This story contains details of sexual violence which some readers may find upsetting
paras.zh: 这个故事包含性暴力的细节，有些读者可能会感到不安

paras.en: "Get out of the car!" screams a woman, accusing a driver of exposing himself and making obscene comments as she walked by. She is filming the scene in a busy Baghdad street on her phone, and the camera captures him resisting her attempts to open the door as she confronts him.
paras.zh: “下车！”一名妇女尖叫起来，指责一名司机暴露自己，并在她走过时发表猥亵言论。她正在巴格达一条繁忙的街道上用手机拍摄这一场景，相机捕捉到他在面对他时抵制她打开门的企图。

paras.en: The video can be seen, with others like it, on the Instagram page of Iraqi women's rights activist Sarah Jassim. She posts them on behalf of women who complain about sexual abuse and harassment by Iraqi men and boys.
paras.zh: 这段视频和其他视频一样，可以在伊拉克女权活动家莎拉·贾西姆（ Sarah Jassim ）的Instagram页面上看到。她代表投诉伊拉克男人和男孩性虐待和性骚扰的女性发布这些信息。

paras.en: "Your camera is your weapon," she tells the BBC. "It's a way to document evidence in case a woman decides to sue her harasser, or at least it is a means to shame him."
paras.zh: “你的相机是你的武器，”她告诉英国广播公司。“这是一种记录证据的方式，以防女人决定起诉她的骚扰者，或者至少这是一种羞辱他的手段。”

paras.en: One of the videos she posted led to the arrest of the alleged perpetrator, a policeman accused of harassing schoolgirls, she says.
paras.zh: 她说，她发布的一段视频导致被指控的肇事者被捕，这名警察被指控骚扰女学生。

paras.en: Jassim says posting the videos is risky both for herself and for the women concerned. We have spoken to numerous victims of sexual abuse in Iraq who say that society often blames the victim.
paras.zh: Jassim说，发布这些视频对她自己和相关女性来说都是危险的。我们与伊拉克的许多性虐待受害者进行了交谈，他们说社会经常责怪受害者。

paras.en: "I have received death threats, and I have also been threatened with acid attacks," Jassim says. "I have been accused of inciting public indecency, because I encourage women to speak in a society that expects us to be silent."
paras.zh: “我收到了死亡威胁，我也受到了酸性攻击的威胁，”贾西姆说。“我被指控煽动公开猥亵，因为我鼓励女性在一个期望我们保持沉默的社会中发言。”

paras.en: She now barely leaves home, for her own safety, and instead spends hours playing with her dog.
paras.zh: 为了自己的安全，她现在几乎不离开家，而是花了几个小时和她的狗玩耍。

paras.en: There is a need for stricter laws, she argues, including laws that explicitly criminalise "harassment" and "gender-based violence" - terms that are currently absent from the penal code.
paras.zh: 她认为，有必要制定更严格的法律，包括明确将“骚扰”和“基于性别的暴力”定为刑事犯罪的法律--目前刑法中没有这些术语。

paras.en: "Recognising the problem is the best way to address it," she says. "We need protection, abusers have to be deterred."
paras.zh: “认识到这个问题是解决问题的最佳方式，”她说。“我们需要保护，必须阻止施虐者。”

paras.en: Many Iraqi women have told the BBC they felt failed by the justice and police systems. Pursuing legal action against a harasser or a rapist is a long path in Iraq, with complicated procedures, and uncertain results, according to a number of activists and lawyers we have spoken to.
paras.zh: 许多伊拉克妇女告诉英国广播公司，她们感到被司法和警察系统辜负了。我们采访过的一些活动人士和律师表示，对骚扰者或强奸者采取法律行动在伊拉克是一条漫长的道路，程序复杂，结果不确定。

paras.en: Violence against women and girls in Iraq is "widespread and under-reported," according to a report in May by a UN committee on discrimination against women, which called for stronger legislation.
paras.zh: 根据联合国歧视妇女问题委员会5月份的一份报告，伊拉克暴力侵害妇女和女孩行为“普遍存在且未得到充分报告” ，该报告呼吁加强立法。

paras.en: Among dozens of recommendations, it urged the authorities to repeal "discriminatory" laws that exonerate rapists if they marry their victims, and allow reduced sentences for murder in cases where a perpetrator was carrying out a so-called "honour killing".
paras.zh: 在数十项建议中，它敦促当局废除“歧视性”法律，这些法律免除强奸犯与受害者结婚的责任，并允许在肇事者实施所谓的“名誉杀人”的情况下，对谋杀罪减刑。

paras.en: Amal - not her real name - has been battling in court for about five years. She accuses her ex-husband of repeatedly raping their daughter - who was under 18 at the time - at gunpoint.
paras.zh: Amal （不是她的真名）已经在法庭上争斗了大约五年。她指责她的前夫在枪口下反复强奸当时未满18岁的女儿。

paras.en: She recalls her daughter's harrowing account of the incident, when she says the father walked into the girl's room and laid his weapon on her bed. She says he told her: "No-one will hear you if I kill you."
paras.zh: 她回忆起女儿对这一事件的悲惨叙述，她说父亲走进女孩的房间，把武器放在她的床上。她说，他告诉她： “如果我杀了你，没有人会听到你的声音。”

paras.en: Sexual abuse has long been seen as a taboo subject in Iraq. I have been in touch with many survivors who say that they prefer to hush it up, because of a potential family backlash. Others told us they were afraid to go to the police, for fear of social stigma and possible harassment. But Amal was determined to seek justice and rushed to police to report the incident.
paras.zh: 长期以来，性虐待一直被视为伊拉克的一个禁忌话题。我一直与许多幸存者保持联系，他们说，由于潜在的家庭反弹，他们更愿意隐瞒。其他人告诉我们，他们害怕报警，因为害怕社会耻辱和可能的骚扰。但Amal决心寻求正义，并急于向警方报告此事件。

paras.en: "She had lots of bruises around her wrists, as he held her hands tight. Whenever she tried to scream, he would cover her mouth with his hands," Amal says.
paras.zh: “她手腕上有很多瘀伤，他紧紧地握着她的手。每当她试图尖叫时，他都会用手捂住她的嘴，” Amal说。

paras.en: Amal showed me medical documents, including DNA evidence, which support her account.
paras.zh: Amal向我展示了医疗文件，包括DNA证据，这些文件支持了她的说法。

paras.en: A further demonstration of her ex-husband's cruelty came, Amal says, when she heard him tell a family member to "wash off our disgrace" if he was arrested. The expression is used in Iraq to refer to so-called honour killings - carried out in the belief that a woman has compromised a family's reputation.
paras.zh: Amal说，当她听到前夫告诉一名家庭成员，如果他被捕，要“洗掉我们的耻辱”时，她进一步证明了她前夫的残忍行为。这个词在伊拉克被用来指所谓的名誉杀人--认为一个女人已经损害了一个家庭的声誉。

paras.en: Amal says she believes the father threatened to put an end to his daughter's life "so the medical report would not be released and the assault would not be proven".
paras.zh: Amal说，她相信父亲威胁要结束他女儿的生命， “所以医疗报告不会公布，袭击也不会得到证实”。

paras.en: She says her ex-husband is on the run and the court case remains open.
paras.zh: 她说，她的前夫正在逃跑，法庭案件仍在审理中。

paras.en: "I fought all alone," says Amal, bursting into tears as she says her ex-husband hired several lawyers but she could not afford legal representation, and her family turned a blind eye to the situation.
paras.zh: Amal说： “我一个人打架。”她说，她的前夫雇佣了几名律师，但她负担不起法律代表，她的家人对这种情况视而不见。

paras.en: She no longer has any faith that a court ruling will come in her favour. "I just want him to stay out of my way forever," she says, with a sigh of despair.
paras.zh: 她不再相信法院的裁决会对她有利。“我只是想让他永远远离我，”她绝望地叹了口气说。

paras.en: Amal's daughter is more fortunate than some women who have experienced domestic sexual abuse in Iraq, as she has a safe place to live.
paras.zh: Amal的女儿比在伊拉克经历过家庭性虐待的一些妇女更幸运，因为她有一个安全的住所。

paras.en: Many survivors have no independent income and nowhere to go. Iraq has very few shelters for abused women.
paras.zh: 许多幸存者没有独立收入，无处可去。伊拉克几乎没有收容受虐妇女的庇护所。

paras.en: Those we know of were established by an organisation co-founded by Yanar Mohammed, an internationally recognised women's rights advocate. Last March she was murdered outside her house in Baghdad by armed men. The perpetrators are still unknown.
paras.zh: 我们所知道的是由国际公认的妇女权利倡导者亚纳尔·穆罕默德（ Yanar Mohammed ）共同创立的一个组织。去年3月，她在巴格达的房子外面被武装人员谋杀。肇事者仍然下落不明。

paras.en: Experts working for the UN Human Rights Council wrote in April that Mohammed had been receiving death threats and online abuse for years, which were "believed to come from extremist religious militia".
paras.zh: 为联合国人权理事会工作的专家在4月份写道，穆罕默德多年来一直受到死亡威胁和网络虐待，这些威胁和虐待“被认为来自极端主义宗教民兵”。

paras.en: Activists repeatedly told us that targeted attacks on their colleagues have been on the rise in recent years.
paras.zh: 活动人士一再告诉我们，近年来针对同事的有针对性的攻击一直在增加。

paras.en: Hanaa Edwar, another prominent women's rights activist, says she saw Mohammed just two days before she was killed. She says she has also been threatened.
paras.zh: 另一位着名的女权活动家哈娜·埃德瓦尔（ Hanaa Edwar ）说，她在穆罕默德被杀前两天才见到她。她说她也受到了威胁。

paras.en: "There are no laws, no protection, and no justice for women in Iraq," she tells me.
paras.zh: 她告诉我： “伊拉克没有法律，没有保护，也没有为妇女伸张正义。”

paras.en: "The problem in Iraq is not that women stay silent. It is that when they speak, very little in the system is built to listen, Mustafa Saadoon, head of the Iraqi Observatory for Human Rights, tells the BBC.
paras.zh: “伊拉克的问题不在于女性保持沉默。伊拉克人权观察组织负责人穆斯塔法·萨杜恩（ Mustafa Saadoon ）告诉英国广播公司，当他们说话时，系统中很少有人倾听。

paras.en: "A woman who reports sexual violence has to get past her family first, then a police station, then a court, and at every one of those doors someone is likely to tell her to settle it quietly."
paras.zh: “一个报告性暴力的女人必须先经过她的家人，然后是警察局，然后是法庭，在每一扇门上，都有人可能会告诉她安静地解决这个问题。”

paras.en: Among the Iraqi women who say they feel failed by the system is Samira - not her real name.
paras.zh: 在伊拉克妇女中，萨米拉不是她的真名，她说她觉得自己被制度辜负了。

paras.en: She tells the BBC that walking in the street puts her on the edge, after repeated harassments.
paras.zh: 她告诉英国广播公司，在反复骚扰之后，走在街上会让她陷入困境。

paras.en: Once, she says a man "was watching a porn movie on his phone and put it in my face" on public transport.
paras.zh: 有一次，她说一个男人“在他的手机上看色情电影，并把它放在我的脸上”在公共交通工具上。

paras.en: In another incident in Baghdad, she says a man once followed her in his car for over 10 minutes. "It was extremely upsetting... I saw a police car. I went over and told them what had happened. They said they didn't have the authority to do anything."
paras.zh: 在巴格达发生的另一起事件中，她说一名男子曾经跟随她开车超过10分钟。“非常沮丧……我看到了一辆警车。我走过去告诉他们发生了什么事。他们说自己无权做任何事情。”

paras.en: Although her mother is loving and supportive, Samira does not share any stories of sexual harassment with her. "If I tell my family, they will immediately ask me not to leave home in order to stay safe," she says.
paras.zh: 虽然她的母亲充满爱和支持，但Samira没有与她分享任何性骚扰的故事。她说： “如果我告诉我的家人，他们会立即要求我不要离开家，以保持安全。”

paras.en: She has lost faith in state institutions: "Many men, including police officers, find nothing wrong with sexual harassment. If you are not a harasser, you are not a man, this is how they see it," she adds.
paras.zh: 她对国家机构失去了信心： “包括警察在内的许多男性认为性骚扰没有任何问题。如果你不是骚扰者，你就不是男人，这就是他们的看法，”她补充道。

paras.en: Many women I spoke to in Iraq even accused police of sexual harassment. I put the accusation to Muqdad Miri, a spokesman for Iraq's interior ministry.
paras.zh: 我在伊拉克采访的许多妇女甚至指责警方性骚扰。我向伊拉克内政部发言人穆克达德·米里（ Muqdad Miri ）提出了指控。

paras.en: "Cases of harassment involving police personnel happen but they are very few. They get a very harsh punishment, up to 10 years in prison and are dismissed," says Miri.
paras.zh: “涉及警察的骚扰案件时有发生，但很少。他们受到非常严厉的惩罚，最高可判处10年监禁并被解雇，” Miri说。

paras.en: I put it to him that some women were now documenting harassment on social media because they were afraid to report it to police. He said they were posting on social media because it was easier than filing an official report, and because doing so has become a common way to draw attention to a cause.
paras.zh: 我告诉他，一些女性现在在社交媒体上记录骚扰，因为她们害怕向警方举报。他说，他们之所以在社交媒体上发帖，是因为这比提交正式报告更容易，而且这样做已经成为吸引人们关注某一事业的常用方式。

paras.en: I also put to him Samira's experience, in which she says an officer told her that he had no authority to stop harassment. Miri said Samira could have filed a complaint against this officer.
paras.zh: 我还向他讲述了萨米拉的经历，她说一名军官告诉她，他无权停止骚扰。Miri说， Samira本可以对这名警官提起诉讼。

paras.en: There are no reliable statistics for sexual violence or harassment in Iraq. Miri told me that police have received about 300 reports of sexual violence since the beginning of the year. However, he accepts that the real number of cases is higher: "Many cases never reach the police because of society, customs and traditions."
paras.zh: 伊拉克没有关于性暴力或性骚扰的可靠统计数据。Miri告诉我，自今年年初以来，警方已收到约300起性暴力报告。然而，他承认案件的实际数量更高： “由于社会、习俗和传统，许多案件从未报警。”

paras.en: The stories of the women the BBC spoke to draw a picture of their battle not just against sexual violence itself, but against deeply entrenched mentalities and social beliefs that allow it to persist.
paras.zh: BBC讲述这些女性的故事，不仅是为了描绘她们与性暴力本身的斗争，也是为了描绘她们与允许性暴力持续存在的根深蒂固的心态和社会信仰的斗争。

paras.en: Edwar has been advocating for women's causes for over 50 years and her assessment is gloomy: "Twenty-three years after Saddam Hussein's regime was brought down, it seems we are going backwards regarding women's rights."
paras.zh: 爱德华50多年来一直倡导妇女事业，她的评价令人沮丧： “萨达姆·侯赛因政权倒台23年后，我们似乎在妇女权利方面倒退了。”

paras.en: But both she and Jassim say they refuse to give up: "If all of us are going to get scared, no-one will change anything," says Sarah.
paras.zh: 但她和Jassim都说他们拒绝放弃： “如果我们所有人都会害怕，没有人会改变任何事情，” Sarah说。

paras.en: If you have been affected by issues involving sexual abuse and violence, you could speak to a health professional or an organisation that offers support. Details of organisations offering advice and support for people in the UK are available from BBC Action Line.
paras.zh: 如果您受到涉及性虐待和暴力的问题的影响，可以咨询卫生专业人员或提供支持的组织。有关为英国人提供建议和支持的组织的详细信息，请访问BBC Action Line。

articles.title: How Paper-Based Friction Materials Power Modern Machinery

paras.en: How Paper-Based Friction Materials Power Modern Machinery

Have you ever wondered what enables everything from roaring construction machinery to agricultural machinery plowing the fields to industrial equipment shuttling through factories—the precise starting, smooth operation, and reliable braking they achieve?

The answer lies in a seemingly insignificant yet crucial core component: friction material. It acts as the "safety guard" and "power link" of machinery, ensuring every brake is safe and effective, and every power transmission is smooth and flawless.

Among the vast family of friction materials, wet friction materials are becoming the new favorite in modern machinery due to their exceptional reliability, safety, and exceptionally long lifespan. Among wet materials, paper-based friction materials stand out as a leading force thanks to their excellent overall performance, cost-effectiveness, and broad application prospects.
Today, let's delve deeper into the fascinating world of this "unsung hero"—paper-based friction materials.
What is Paper-Based Friction Material? — A Sponge-Like Power Core
Imagine a "sponge" with countless tiny pores—that's the most intuitive image of paper-based friction material.

It is a material with a reticular porous structure composed of three core components: reinforcing fibers, functional fillers, and a binder resin. This unique structure gives it extraordinary capabilities:
- Oil Storage Capacity: The porous structure acts like a miniature "oil depot," capable of storing large quantities of lubricant.

- Dynamic Lubrication: When the friction plate and mating plate engage and are subjected to pressure, the lubricant within the material is instantly squeezed onto the friction surface, forming a tough lubricant film, enabling smooth, gentle "wet" friction.
- Self-Recovery: When the friction plates separate, the material rebounds like memory foam, "absorbing" the lubricant back into the pores, ready for the next operation.

It is this dynamic cycle of "oil storage-oil squeezing-oil return" that allows paper-based friction materials to perform well in an oil bath environment, achieving a perfect combination of high durability and stable friction performance.
Exploring Core Performance: How Do Three Key Factors Affect It?

The performance of paper-based friction materials is not static. Like a top athlete, its performance is influenced by the "field," "equipment," and "condition." Let's examine how these three key factors shape its performance.
Factor 1: The "Stage Effect" of Lubricants

Paper-based friction materials are highly sensitive to lubricants, and different lubricants create distinct "stages" for their performance. Even the same friction material can exhibit significantly different friction characteristics (especially the kinetic friction coefficient) when exposed to different lubricants.
Figure 1: Kinetic friction coefficient curve for a paper-based friction material in gear oil
Figure 2: Dynamic friction coefficient curve of the same material in hydraulic oil

Interpretation: The above chart clearly shows that the same material behaves very differently in gear oil and hydraulic fluid. Furthermore, various additives added to lubricating oils (such as dispersants and anti-wear agents) can interact complexly with the material surface, further affecting its friction properties. Therefore, choosing the right oil for paper-based friction materials is the first step in achieving optimal performance.
Density is a trump card for paper-based friction materials. It is directly related to the material's porosity, leading to a delicate balancing act in terms of performance.

High density (low porosity) means a denser material, resulting in better strength and thermal conductivity, lower wear rate, and longer life. However, the downside is reduced oil storage capacity, which can lead to a lower coefficient of friction and compromise power transmission.

Low density (high porosity) means the material is more porous, resulting in greater oil storage capacity and a higher coefficient of friction, which can provide greater braking force or transmit torque. However, the downside is reduced mechanical strength and wear resistance, shortening service life.
Figure 3: Comparison of the dynamic coefficient of friction for materials of varying densities (Type 2 to Type 6, increasing density)
Figure 4: Comparison of wear rates of materials with different densities

Interpretation: Figures 3 and 4 vividly illustrate this balancing act. There's no such thing as absolute good or bad, only suitability. When selecting a paper-based friction material, the optimal trade-off between friction coefficient and durability must be determined based on specific application requirements (e.g., high torque versus long life).
Factor 3: Extreme Challenges of Operating Conditions

In addition to oil type and density, actual operating conditions, such as surface pressure, sliding speed, and oil temperature, pose extreme challenges to paper-based friction materials. These factors directly affect the temperature of the friction interface, the thickness and stability of the oil film, and thus dynamically alter the coefficient of friction.

Therefore, please remember: the coefficient of friction of a particular paper-based friction material is not a fixed value, but rather a performance range determined through extensive and repeated testing under specific operating conditions.
Broad Applications: Injecting a Powerful "Heart" into Machinery

Thanks to its excellent overall performance and customizability, Carlisle Brake & Friction's paper-based friction materials have been successfully applied to the core components of various heavy-duty machinery, becoming their powerful and reliable "heart."
We understand that different machines and applications require significantly different friction materials. For example:
- Service brakes for construction machinery (such as excavators and loaders) require materials that provide a stable, powerful braking force under high loads to ensure safety.
- Powershift transmissions for agricultural machinery (such as tractors) require materials that provide smooth engagement and excellent heat resistance to handle frequent shifting.
- Clutches for industrial machinery require materials that respond quickly and have a long lifespan to ensure continuous and efficient operation of production lines.

To this end, Carlisle Brake & Friction has developed a series of special paper-based friction materials for different application scenarios, providing each customer with the most suitable and reliable solution.
Continuous Innovation, Driving the Future
Technological advancement is endless. To meet increasingly demanding application requirements and broaden market prospects, Carlisle Brake & Friction remains at the forefront of innovation.

We are not only continuously optimizing the formulation and processing of paper-based friction materials to push their performance limits, but are also actively exploring next-generation wet friction materials with even higher performance. These R&D efforts have made significant progress, aiming to provide global customers with more diverse and advanced options, driving the infinite possibilities of future machinery.

articles.title: Protecting Your Technicians: The Best Ability Is Availability
articles.author: Pro Spot International

paras.en: When we talk about safety in the collision repair industry, the conversation often centers on obvious hazards: welding temperatures, sparks, fumes, electricity, sharp metal, and the importance of wearing the proper personal protective equipment. Those risks are critical to address, but there is another category of safety that can be easier to overlook because the damage isn’t always immediate: ergonomics.

Collision repair is physically demanding work. Technicians spend hours lifting, reaching, bending, twisting, kneeling, working overhead, and handling heavy equipment. The cumulative effect of those movements can take a serious toll over time. In fact, roughly 20%—or 1 out of every 5—of all reported non-fatal injuries in this sector are attributed to repetitive motion or cumulative trauma (Bureau of Labor Statistics).

That statistic is a reminder that technician safety isn’t just about preventing the accident that happens today. It’s also about reducing the physical strain that can contribute to injuries over weeks, months, and years. The best shops should constantly be asking: How can we make this job safer and easier for the technician?
Invest in Your Technicians with Ergonomic Equipment
A technician’s body is one of the most important tools in the shop. Just like any other piece of equipment, it needs to be taken care of.

Consider the number of times a technician may use a spot welding gun throughout a typical day. Spot welders can be heavy, and holding that weight repeatedly—especially while reaching into awkward areas of a vehicle—can put significant stress on the shoulders, arms, wrists, and back.
One individual weld may not seem like a major physical challenge. Hundreds of welds performed over the course of a day are a different story. This is where

ergonomic equipment can make a meaningful difference. Instead of asking a technician to carry and support the full weight of a welding gun throughout the repair, equipment such as Pro Spot’s Ergo Lift Assist can help support the gun and reduce the physical load on the technician.

The technician still controls the equipment and performs the repair, but the equipment helps carry some of the burden. A technician should be focused on getting the correct weld, following the OEM procedure, preparing the metal properly, and completing a quality repair—not thinking about how much their shoulders hurt from holding a welding gun all afternoon.

Ergonomics doesn’t have to mean completely redesigning a shop. Sometimes the biggest improvements come from looking at the repetitive tasks technicians perform every day and asking where unnecessary physical effort can be eliminated.
How often are technicians lifting heavy tools?
How often are they reaching across a vehicle?
Are they bending or kneeling when the job could be positioned differently?
Are tools balanced and easy to maneuver?
Could an assist device support some of the weight?
These questions can identify opportunities to make a technician’s workday safer and more comfortable.
And because these movements are repeated hundreds or thousands of times over a career, even a small reduction in physical strain can have a significant long-term impact.
PPE and Safe Work Practices Still Matter
Ergonomics is only one part of a comprehensive safety program.

Technicians still need the proper personal protective equipment for the job, including appropriate eye and face protection, gloves, hearing protection, respiratory protection, and other PPE when required.

Welding equipment should be properly maintained and operated according to manufacturer instructions. Technicians should understand the hazards associated with welding, sparks, heat, fumes, electricity, and the materials they are working with.
OEM repair procedures should also be followed carefully. The right equipment and ergonomic setup don’t replace proper training or safe work practices.
Instead, ergonomics should complement them.
A truly safe shop addresses both the immediate hazards of the job and the long-term physical demands placed on the people performing it.
Protect the Technician, Protect the Business
Keeping technicians safe isn’t just the right thing to do. It also makes good business sense.
Skilled collision repair technicians are difficult to replace. When a technician is unavailable because of an injury or chronic physical strain, the impact can extend well beyond that individual.

Production can slow down. Other technicians may have to pick up the additional workload. Repair schedules can be affected. And the shop loses the experience and expertise of someone who may have spent years developing their skills.
Investing in ergonomics is an investment in keeping those technicians healthy and productive.
It can also send an important message to employees: We value you enough to invest in making your job safer and easier.
There’s an old saying in sports: “The best ability is availability.”
The same principle applies in the body shop.

Even the best technicians can’t perform at their best if they’re constantly dealing with fatigue, soreness, or an injury. No shop benefits from equipment or processes that unnecessarily wear down the people who rely on them every day.
The objective isn’t to make technicians work harder. It’s to give them the tools and environment they need to work smarter, safer, and more efficiently.

Ergonomic equipment such as lift assists can take some of the physical burden out of repetitive tasks. Proper PPE and safety practices help protect technicians from the immediate hazards of the shop. Together, they create an environment where technicians can focus their energy on what matters most: performing high-quality repairs.
Because protecting your technicians isn’t just about keeping them safe today.
It’s about keeping them healthy, productive, and available to do their best work tomorrow.

articles.title: Hurricane Isias moves toward Gulf Coast, here’s how to prepare and collision assistance available
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: Hurricane Isias is expected to bring heavy rainfall to the central U.S. Gulf Coast and much of the Southeast Friday and into the weekend, according to the National Hurricane Center (NHC).
NHC told the area to prepare for considerable flash and urban flooding, along with significant river flooding, gusty winds, and areas of heavy rain in the western portion of the Yucatan Peninsula.
To get ready for Isaias, GEICO urges customers in the storm’s potential path to take these steps:
- “Follow guidance from local emergency officials, including any evacuation orders.
- “Create an evacuation plan ahead of time. Identify a safe place outside the storm’s path and designate a key contact to share evacuation plans.
- “Move vehicles out of low-lying areas. Vehicles that aren’t being used to evacuate should be moved away from areas prone to heavy flooding. If possible, use a garage or covered parking.
- “Fill the tank. Make sure all vehicles have a full tank of gas.
- “Build a disaster kit. Include three days of water, medications, toiletries, charging cables, blankets, batteries, and a radio. Add food as needed, plus supplies for pets.
- “Identify a safe place for key vehicle documents. If you need to file a claim, have your vehicle title, registration, and any lienholder information handy.”

Consumers are encouraged to download insurance company mobile apps to access policy documents and file a claim, according to a GEICO press release. Consumers may also want to add insurance company 800 numbers to their contacts.
After a storm, consumers should use extreme caution as wind and flooding damage could be severe. The insurance company notes that cars may have been submerged in floodwaters that have since receded.
“Don’t try to drive a vehicle you suspect was flooded,” the release adds.
It also warns consumers to stay away from their vehicle if downed power lines are nearby.
Consumers should leave their vehicles in place if heavy debris, such as a tree limb, falls on them, the release adds. It says the debris could pose a safety risk.

“In situations with major safety risks, GEICO’s claims team will work with customers and come directly to them to inspect a vehicle that isn’t drivable,” the release states. “Customers just need to file a claim first, and GEICO will then work with them to set up a field inspection appointment as quickly as possible.”
The Collision Industry Foundation (CIF) is a resource the industry can request emergency relief from after catastrophic events such as a hurricane.
Resources are available to anyone who works in the industry. This includes individuals working in shops or in supporting roles outside of a shop.
The organization does not provide funds for businesses. However, a business owner can apply for funds for items, like personally owned tools.
To apply for assistance, click here. Businesses may wish to broadcast the resource to any employee or family impacted by the storm.
Individuals and business owners can also apply for assistance if they’ve lost personal property, such as a house, from a disaster.
To give a tax-exempt donation to the nonprofit, click here or text 734-366-4990. Donations can be made once, monthly, quarterly, or annually.
CIF is also running a “$25 for 25” donation campaign to celebrate their 25th anniversary.

“Meaningful change doesn’t require a massive contribution — it just takes a community standing together,” a social media post from CIF states. “We’re rallying 1,000 individual technicians, estimators, shop owners, and suppliers to donate $25 in honor of CIF’s 25th anniversary. Together, we can build a rock-solid safety net for colleagues recovering from natural disasters and life-altering emergencies.”
